title: Metering determinism during preemptible GPU evictions and graceful resume for reserved capacity
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Reserved GPU pools may experience preemptible evictions (cloud spot interruptions, host maintenance, or node preemption). When an inference process is preempted mid-request or mid-batch and subsequently retried on another worker, current metering semantics risk double-counting tokens or failing to attribute usage to the original lease. This leads to billing inaccuracies for reserved customers and noisy quota consumption metrics.

Goal: Design and implement a deterministic metering/ledger strategy that guarantees single-count billing for unique inference work across eviction/transfer boundaries, supports graceful resume semantics for in-flight KV caches, and allows fast reconciliation of orphaned inflight items after host failures. Approach should minimize latency impact and be compatible with existing rolling-window and monthly quota resets.
acceptance_criteria: Idempotent request footprint: Replayed/retied requests with identical idempotency keys must not increment token counters more than once; verified by unit and integration tests against simulated preemptions.

Lease checkpoints: Worker checkpoints for long-running streaming responses persist minimal lease metadata (request_id, last-counted-token-index, kv-cache-checksum) to durable store within 1s of progress to allow deterministic resume.

Reconciliation job: A background reconciler must detect orphaned checkpoints from preempted workers and either reattach them to resumed workers or roll them into a safe credit adjustment audit log within 5 minutes of eviction events.
No user-visible latency regression: End-to-end 95th percentile tail latency for hosted reserved requests increases by less than 5% in the common non-eviction path.

Auditability: Every meter event related to a resumed or reconciled request must include reason tags (eviction-retry, resumed-from-checkpoint, reconciler-adjustment) and a pointer to the eviction incident id for billing investigations.

Compatibility with rolling resets: Reconciled adjustments for requests that span quota window boundaries must be anchored to the original request's quota epoch so month/day boundaries reconcile correctly.
Test coverage: Integration test harness that simulates preemption and verifies ledger invariants across three cloud regions included in CI gate.
Operational runbook: Runbook describing how to inspect reconciler decisions, force-safe-rollbacks, and create invoice adjustments is committed to Confluence and linked in ticket.
Security review: Solution approved by security team with notes on durable store access and encryption-at-rest for checkpoint metadata.

design_notes: Prefer append-only ledger entries for adjustments rather than destructive edits to past invoiceable counters. Checkpoint metadata kept minimal to reduce hot writes. Consider probabilistic checkpoint backoff under high throughput to avoid write amplification.
implementation_plan: 1) Add idempotency key plumbing for every slice/stream; 2) Durable checkpoint API + lightweight worker hook; 3) Reconciler service that subscribes to eviction events and inspects recent checkpoints; 4) Billing adapter that converts reconciler decisions into audit-only adjustments flagged for human review for first 2 weeks; 5) Observability (meters, traces, reconciler decisions).
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency, integration tests in CI with simulated spot evictions, chaos test where 1% of requests are force-evicted, and load test to verify p95 tail latency impact <5%.
